findings.reason: Level 4 is not justified by admissible evidence — the row's own G1 note concedes it: 'smallholder reach figures are vendor-reported - scale rung cannot rest on them.' findings.proposed_value: No all-practice national CSA adoption rate exists. Practice-specific (labelled, admissible): raised-bed wheat cultivation — named a 'widely adopted CSA practice' in FAO's Towards Climate-Smart Agriculture in Egypt (CA report, sec. 3.1.5) — tripled from 113,500 ha (MY2013/14) to 334,000 ha (MY2016/17) across the four major wheat governorates (Sharqia, Beheira, Kafr El Sheikh, Dakahlia), ~26% of the 1.26M-ha national wheat area (USDA FAS GAIN, Mar 2017); MALR/ARC target 420,000 ha by MY2020/21 (USDA GAIN, Mar 2020). T2 corroboration, divergent estimates: ~125,000 ha / 10% of national wheat area by 2017 (Gamal et al., Food Security 2018, doi:10.1007/s12571-018-0794-3); 19.3% of wheat area under raised beds in a three-province survey (Agric. Water Mgmt 2021, S0378377421000676).
findings.reason: The gap is refutable with labelled practice-specific evidence the assessor missed by searching only 'CSA adoption' phrasings. I verified verbatim in the USDA GAIN 2017 primary PDF: 'Raised bed cultivation has about tripled from 113,500 ha in MY2013/14 to 334,000 ha in MY 2016/17' against a 1.26M-ha national wheat area stated in the same report (~26%). Raised-bed/wide-ridge cultivation is explicitly a CSA practice per FAO's own Egypt CSA report (which I full-text scanned — confirming the assessor's correct claim that THAT report has no adoption statistic; the only 'adoption rate' sentence there is a Kenya/Tanzania study). Row 1.5 sets the workbook's own precedent that commodity-specific labelled figures are admissible as Documented when no single national rate exists; the same rule fills this cell. Caveats for the assessor: single practice, single crop, vintage 2017 (stale-flag mandatory), and the T2 (10%) vs T4-carried MALR/ARC (26%) estimates diverge — record as a labelled Documented value, not a single number; level derivation left to the ladder. GAIN is a US-government analytical report on Egypt, so T4 (reputable grey) is the honest anchor tier, with T2 corroboration; year 2017.

findings.proposed_value: No national share with provenance exists. findings.reason: Internal-consistency refutation: the assessor's own trail names IFPRI DP 2359 and dismisses it as 'two-governorate survey data only', but the workbook's own rows 1.6 (Upper Egypt 6% contract farming, seven governorates), 1.7 (rural 2.3% formal borrowing) and 5.4 (this very same Minya/Beni Suef survey) all admit regional labelled survey constructs as Documented when no national figure exists — 1.6 and 1.7 even assign level 1 on them. The assessor was right to refute the prior's constructed composite (platform counts / holdings denominator) — but replacing a bad composite with a Gap when an admissible labelled T2 survey statistic exists is inconsistent with the instrument's own precedent. Either 8.9 becomes Documented/T2/2023/level 1 (2-3% is far below any plausible L2 floor, parallel to 1.6/1.7), or 1.6/1.7 must revert to Gap; the disagreement should be resolved the first way. Single-source flag applies.

The presence facts the assessor logged in the note (CCIC daily warnings, Bashaer) are correctly kept out of the value. Gap legitimate.

EGY-gap.protocol_issues: Cross-row consistency is the main G2 issue surfaced by this pass: the instrument's treatment of regional labelled survey constructs is inconsistent — admitted as Documented (with levels) in 1.6, 1.7 and 5.4, but treated as grounds for Gap in 8.9 despite the identical evidence class (same IFPRI survey as 5.4). A written rule on when a regional labelled construct fills a national indicator (vs. records as Gap) would remove this class of disagreement. Second, gap-search phrasing sensitivity: the 1.8 miss arose because searches used indicator-object phrasing ('CSA adoption rate') and never practice-level phrasing ('raised bed', 'laser levelling', 'deficit irrigation') — the protocol's search-trail requirement could usefully mandate at least one decomposed practice/component-level phrasing per gap. Third, tier-lookup edge case: foreign-government analytical reports on the assessed country (USDA FAS GAIN) fit neither 'T3 government artefacts' (they are not Egyptian instruments) nor cleanly the T4 examples list — I treated them as T4; worth adding to the domain lookup (fas.usda.gov → T4). Fourth, minor: openknowledge.fao.org and icarda.org bitstream/page URLs return 403 to non-browser fetchers, so A10 spot-resolution of those deep links needs a browser UA — the links themselves are live (verified by download).

findings.reason: Gap is fillable with a resolvable measured artefact the search trail missed.
